correctness.rationale: The given two-step group law preserves the stated lattice, and degree-preserving vertex relabelings with the induced edge signs preserve both it and the bracket. Equivariant rational Nomizu reduces the claim to the nine-generator CE complex (negating all central dual generators accommodates the usual minus convention). An independently written exact replay builds all 512 wedges, checks d²=0 and commutation with the signed involutions, and reproduces all ranks and all ten character rows by computing plus/minus cohomology and inverting the Klein-four character matrix. The ranks in degrees 0–8 are (0,5,14,31,46,31,14,5,0). Direct invariant orbit sums give all three stated quotient vectors, of totals 108, 110 and 54; these are rational geometric-quotient Betti numbers by equivariant triangulation and averaging, not an assertion of freeness. The hub action has determinants (-1,-1) on vertices and center; the tip action has (-1,+1), checking the top-degree asymmetry.
residual_risks: Replay verifies finite rational linear algebra, not integral torsion or cup products; neither is claimed.

value.rationale: The two graph-theoretically inequivalent exchanges in the diamond give a natural test of how vertex symmetries change rational cohomology. The exact character answers that question in every degree and permits every subgroup quotient to be treated without new cochain computations. In particular, the two geometric involution quotients already differ in b₂ (9 versus 10), not just by the predictable top-degree orientation distinction. This is a usable equivariant benchmark, not an ordinary Betti-table recomputation.
residual_risks: The value is an exact invariant of a specific natural graph; no general recurrence or assertion about cup products is justified.
